bio: Faizan Malik is the founder of Culture Shawq Entertainment Club, a stand-up comedy club in Pakistan.

A mechanical engineer by degree, he studied Mechanical Engineering in the USA and began doing stand-up comedy in a coffee shop as a side hustle. After returning to Pakistan, he started his own comedy club.

summary: In Episode 27 (Season 2) of the Muffled Minds Podcast, host Khawar Shahzad sits down with Faizan Malik, founder of Culture Shawq Entertainment Club, a stand-up comedy club in Pakistan. A mechanical engineer by degree, Faizan studied at Michigan State University in the USA, started doing stand-up at an open mic in a coffee shop in East Lansing, and after returning to Pakistan in 2023, started his own comedy club. The episode opens with a teaser of his sharpest lines, then traces the whole journey from engineering to comedy.

Faizan explains why he chose mechanical engineering, how comedy began as a healthy distraction that turned unhealthy, and how the name Culture Shawq came from the culture shock he felt going back and forth between Pakistan and America. He talks about starting a club from zero in a country with no bars, no third spaces and no infrastructure for stand-up, and about the mindset and resistance he faced, on stage and off. The conversation then turns to the stage drama artists who came before him, and to Aftab Iqbal, who took stage actors into commercial television, gave them family-friendly shows and movie roles, and had to move his show to the UAE when politics got involved.

The episode compares comedy in India and Pakistan, where India has bars, a third space and an entertainment industry tied to Bollywood, while Pakistan has no proper place for stand-up and an audience that often takes crowd work personally. It closes on comedy and mental health, with Faizan speaking openly about his own anxiety, insomnia medication and the stigma around antidepressants, and on the future of Culture Shawq, before a rapid-fire round on biryani, bombing on stage and scripted versus spontaneous comedy.

takeaways: Comedy started for Faizan as a healthy distraction from engineering, and then turned into a very unhealthy distraction.
Culture Shawq is a bilingual double entendre: culture shock, spelled with a Q, from the shock he felt going back and forth between Pakistan and America.
The biggest difficulty in starting a comedy club in Pakistan is the psychology of people and their mindset, on stage and off stage.
Aftab Iqbal changed the trend by taking stage actors into commercial shows, giving them family comedy, clean comedy and movie roles.
India is way ahead infrastructurally because it has bars and third spaces to perform in, while Pakistan has no proper place for stand-up.
In India the audience accepts crowd work and enjoys it, while in Pakistan the audience often takes it personally.
Faizan speaks openly about his own anxiety and insomnia medication, and says mental health should be taken seriously, with a proper checkup.
Writing is always superior to spontaneity in stand-up comedy, because if you only rely on spontaneous stuff you will have nothing as a writer.
Discipline beats talent: if the talent works hard, Faizan would still go with discipline.
